8.1a — Boss Design: Spec It First

"Sorta their first on their own experience" — this is the capstone. The mistake every first-time boss builder makes: start with the boss's SIZE. Today you start with its SPEC — a one-page design document, in words, that a stranger could build from.

Concept Lab ~25 min

A boss is a conversation: it asks a question with an attack, the player answers with a move, and the boss listens (takes

The spec sheet (write all six, today, on paper):

  1. Identity (1 sentence): "The Cave Warden: slow, huge, guards the exit; telegraphs everything."
  2. Health economy: boss HP vs. how many hits your player can deal (8.3a) vs. player HP 3. Aim: a fight of 60–90 seconds. Do the arithmetic NOW: hits needed × seconds between openings = fight length
  3. Phases (2 or 3): what changes at each threshold — new attack? faster? arena change? Each phase must be readable by the player within one exchange
  4. Attacks (2–3 per phase max), each with: telegraph (what tells you it is coming — wind-up frames, a flash), timing (how long to react), counterplay (the move that beats it), and punishment (what a mistake costs)
  5. Tells & fairness: same rule as 7.5a signposting — the boss is a level that fights back, so it must be readable
  6. Arena: reuse your Unit 6 "room" shape: two exits becomes one exit (the door only opens when the boss dies); hazards the BOSS ignores but the player must respect

Socratic

The AP exam's Create PT asks you to justify design decisions in writing. Boss specs ARE that skill. Why does writing the spec BEFORE the code make the coding shorter — and what kind of bug does a spec prevent (hint: the kind where the boss is simultaneously too strong to lose to and too boring to win against)?

Design Lab ~20 min

Stress-test the spec with the enemy state machine. Your boss is 4.5a's machine with more states. Map it — states as boxes, thresholds on the arrows:

IDLE (2s) → ATTACK 1 (telegraph 0.6s, strike, recover 1s)
    → IDLE → ATTACK 2 ...
HP <= 50%  → PHASE 2 (attack cooldown 2s → 1.2s, adds ATTACK 3)
HP <= 20%  → PHASE 3 (speed 2 → 3, arena hazard activates)
HP <= 0    → DEAD (door opens)

Count your boxes: a boss with 6 states is a big build; with 12 it will not exist by January. Cut states until it is buildable, not until it is impressive. You can always add a phase after it WORKS — and never before.

The one question that catches bad specs: for each attack, what does the player DO? If the answer is "dodge randomly" or "take the hit," the attack is decoration. Every attack needs its counterplay sentence: "jump over the shockwave; the jump is possible because the wave is 1 tile tall and your jump is 2."

Bug Hunt: Spec review

  1. Swap specs with a partner. They play the boss IN THEIR HEAD against your attack list — ask them to say the counterplay for each. Any attack they cannot answer is under-designed.
  2. Check the arithmetic: if the player can deal damage only 1 second out of every 5, and the boss needs 20 hits... what is the FIGHT LENGTH? Over 90 seconds means cut HP or add openings.
  3. Phase 3 adds speed AND a hazard AND a new attack. How many new things did you introduce at once — what does 7.5a say about that number?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Commit the design

  1. Type the final spec as BOSS_SPEC.md in your repo root, next to the code it will govern. Design docs live WITH the project.
  2. Sketch the arena on paper (reuse the Unit 6 room); mark where the player enters, where the boss idles, and the door that stays shut.
  3. Commit + push: "8.1a: boss spec + arena sketch".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Write a six-part boss spec: identity, economy, phases, attacks, tells, arena
  • Do the health arithmetic and defend the fight length
  • Map the boss as a state machine with thresholds on the arrows
  • Answer "what does the player DO?" for every single attack
